relevant_acts: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 — Section 4 (right to claim maintenance)
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 — Section 5 (application to Tribunal)
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 — Section 9 (order for maintenance)
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 — Section 23 (transfer of property to be void in certain circumstances)
institution_rules: The applicant must be a parent (biological, adoptive, or step-parent) or a senior citizen (60 years or above, including those without children) unable to maintain themselves from their own earnings or property; the application may be filed by the senior citizen personally, or, if they are unable to do so, by any person or a registered voluntary organisation with their consent, or the Tribunal may act suo motu. Name the specific children/relatives from whom maintenance is claimed and their relationship, describe the applicant's income/assets and needs, and the respondent's capacity to pay. Parties are ordinarily not entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner before the Tribunal as of right under Section 5(4) — draft the application in plain, self-explanatory language suitable for the applicant to present in person, while still following the required structure. Do NOT state a fixed statutory ceiling on the monthly maintenance amount — the amount actually payable depends on the Tribunal's assessment of needs and the respondent's means, and any cap that may exist under the Act or State rules has been the subject of conflicting judicial interpretation; use [VERIFY: applicable maintenance ceiling, if any, under this State's rules] rather than asserting a figure. If the senior citizen transferred property to the respondent subject to an express or implied condition of being maintained, and the respondent has failed to provide such maintenance, mention this specifically as it may allow the Tribunal to declare the transfer void under Section 23. Attach proof of age, proof of relationship, income/asset details, and any documents evidencing the transfer of property if Section 23 relief is sought. NEVER invent a specific maintenance figure — use the amount stated by the client or [VERIFY]. Note that an appeal against the Tribunal's order lies to the Appellate Tribunal within 60 days under Section 16. For offences and procedures after 1 July 2024, cite the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) — NOT the repealed IPC 1860, CrPC 1973, or Indian Evidence Act 1872, if any related criminal conduct (e.g. abandonment under Section 24) is also being referenced. If unsure of a new-code section number, use [VERIFY].
